parents.title: Toxic Beliefs Parents Teach Children
parents.intro: Please check any message you received from a parent or caretaker while growing up.

items: Told me I was bad or worthless
Made me feel I wasn’t good enough
Constantly criticized me, or were extremely negative
Called me names, or said I was dumb or stupid
Made fun of me, or “put me down” in front of others
Told me I’d never make anything of myself
Constantly compared me to my brothers or sisters
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: Never really accepted me, or made me feel unwanted
Made me feel I didn’t belong in the family
Told me they wished I’d never been born
Seemed to like my brother or sister better
Rarely hugged me or told me they loved me
Abandoned me, or died, when I was young
Divorced when I was a child
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: Neglected me physically
Neglected me emotionally, or didn’t care how I felt
Were rarely around, or too busy to pay attention to me
Abused me physically, or beat me with objects
Sexually molested me
Frightened me a lot
Did not provide a safe home for me
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: Were extremely controlling, or acted like dictators
Used guilt, money, or threats to control me
Couldn’t stand it if I disagreed with them
Didn’t allow me to express my feelings
Made my decisions for me, or made me feel helpless
Were overprotective, or kept me away from other children
Taught me the world is scary and to expect the worst
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: Got drunk or used drugs
Fought a lot, including about money
Were depressed or unavailable because of illness
Behavior was odd, unusual, or bizarre
Were unreliable, inconsistent, or couldn’t be trusted
Taught me not to trust anyone
Lied, cheated others, or broke the law
Made me keep family secrets, or pretended all was fine
Made me take care of them, or blamed me for their problems
Rarely admitted mistakes or said they were sorry
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: Pressured me and expected too much of me
Were overly concerned about grades
Were very concerned about my looks and clothes
Were very concerned about money and “status”
Were extremely conservative and legalistic
Made me feel ashamed of myself, or of them
Tried to make me think they were perfect
Spoiled me, or let me do whatever I wanted
Constantly bragged about me to others
Made me feel “special” or “unique”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

parents.note: Some of these messages may seem harmless, or even kind. Yet even well-meant messages can teach beliefs that cause pain later in life. What was learned can be examined, questioned, and replaced with truth.
parents.verse: “Though my father and mother forsake me, the LORD will receive me.”

media.title: Toxic Messages from Media & Culture
media.intro: Please check any message you have absorbed from TV, movies, music, advertising, or social media.

items: “Your worth depends on how you look.”
“Thin (or muscular) is beautiful; anything else is failure.”
“Aging is something to hide or fight.”
“Everyone else looks better than you.”
“Fix your appearance and your life will be better.”
“Filtered, edited images are what normal looks like.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe?

items: “You are what you achieve.”
“More money and possessions will make you happy.”
“If you’re not successful by a certain age, you’ve failed.”
“Rest is laziness; always be productive.”
“Important people are famous, wealthy, or followed.”
“What you own shows who you are.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe?

items: “Everyone else’s life is better than yours.”
“Your value is measured in likes and followers.”
“If it isn’t posted, it didn’t matter.”
“You must always be available and connected.”
“Missing out means being left behind.”
“Others’ highlight reels are their real lives.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe?

items: “The right person will complete you.”
“If love takes work, it isn’t real love.”
“Romance should always feel exciting.”
“Your worth depends on being desired.”
“Commitment is a trap.”
“Being single means something is wrong with you.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe?

items: “Go for the gusto.”
“It doesn’t get any better than this.”
“You only live once, so enjoy it now.”
“Treat yourself; you deserve it.”
“Alcohol makes you fun, relaxed, or accepted.”
“If it feels good, do it.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe?

items: “You should always be happy.”
“Follow your heart; your feelings are always right.”
“You deserve whatever you want.”
“Your truth is whatever feels right to you.”
“Anyone who disagrees with you is against you.”
“Instant results are normal; waiting is failure.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe?

items: “Faith is outdated or unintelligent.”
“Christians are hypocrites, so faith isn’t real.”
“Right and wrong are just personal opinions.”
“God, if He exists, is distant or uninvolved.”
“Spiritual things don’t matter in real life.”
“Sin is just a word for having fun.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe?

items: “The world is more dangerous than ever.”
“Disaster is always around the corner.”
“You can’t trust anyone.”
“People who are different are a threat.”
“Nothing will ever get better.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe?

media.note: Some of these messages sound harmless, or even encouraging. Yet repeated often enough, they can quietly shape what we believe about ourselves, others, and God. What was absorbed can be examined, questioned, and replaced with truth.
media.verse: “Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind.”

partners.title: Toxic Messages from Spouses or Partners
partners.intro: Please check any message you have received from a spouse or partner, in words or through actions.

items: “You can’t do anything right.”
“You’re stupid.”
“You’re lucky anyone would have you.”
“You’re a terrible parent.”
“You’ll never change.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “Why can’t you be more like…?”
“You’ve let yourself go.”
“You’re too sensitive.”
“You always…” or “You never…”
“Nothing you do is ever enough.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “It’s your fault I’m angry.”
“You made me do it.”
“If you were a better spouse, I wouldn’t have to…”
“You’re the problem in this marriage.”
“My unhappiness is your fault.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “I don’t love you anymore.”
“I’m only staying because of the kids.”
“Your needs aren’t important.”
“I don’t find you attractive.”
Silence or affection withheld as punishment
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “You don’t need your friends or family.”
“I decide how the money is spent.”
“You need my permission.”
“Don’t tell anyone about our problems.”
“Your opinions don’t matter.”
Constant checking on where you are and who you’re with
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “If you leave, you’ll regret it.”
“I’ll take the kids.”
“No one will believe you.”
“You’ll never make it on your own.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “God says you must submit to whatever I say.”
“A good Christian spouse wouldn’t complain.”
“You have to forgive and forget, right now.”
“Leaving would be a sin, no matter what I do.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “I only do this because I love you.”
“I was just joking; you can’t take a joke.”
“No one will ever love you like I do.”
“I know what’s best for you.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

partners.note: Hurtful messages from someone close to us can slowly become beliefs about ourselves. What was absorbed can be examined, questioned, and replaced with truth.
extra: If you feel afraid of your spouse or partner, help is available 24 hours a day.
National Domestic Violence Hotline: 1-800-799-7233 • Text START to 88788 • thehotline.org

church-setting.title: Toxic Messages from Church & Religion
church-setting.intro: Please check any message you were taught, directly or indirectly, in a church or religious setting.

items: “God is angry and waiting to punish you.”
“God loves you only when you obey.”
“God is disappointed in you.”
“God is distant and uninvolved in your life.”
“God loves some people more than others.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about God or yourself?

items: “You must earn God’s forgiveness.”
“Some sins are too big to be forgiven.”
“If you sin again, your repentance wasn’t real.”
“You must keep paying for your past.”
“You can never be good enough for God.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about God or yourself?

items: “A good Christian keeps all the rules.”
“Your worth depends on how much you serve.”
“Being busy at church means being spiritual.”
“Appearances matter more than the heart.”
“Doubting means you have no faith.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about God or yourself?

items: “Christians shouldn’t feel depressed or anxious.”
“If you had enough faith, you wouldn’t struggle.”
“Counseling or medication shows a lack of faith.”
“Anger is always a sin.”
“Just pray about it, and it will go away.”
“Emotional struggles are a sign of spiritual weakness.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about God or yourself?

items: “Suffering means God is punishing you.”
“If you’re faithful, God will make you healthy and prosperous.”
“Bad things happen because of hidden sin.”
“Christians should always be joyful and never grieve.”
“Unanswered prayer means God doesn’t care.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about God or yourself?

items: “Never question church leaders.”
“Leaders speak for God, so they can’t be wrong.”
“Your own needs don’t matter.”
“Keep family problems secret to protect the church.”
“Being submissive means accepting mistreatment.”
“Leaving a church means leaving God.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about God or yourself?

items: “You are nothing but a worthless sinner.”
“Your body and sexuality are shameful.”
“Past sexual sin leaves you permanently damaged.”
“Enjoying life is selfish or sinful.”
“People outside the church are the enemy.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about God or yourself?

items: “If you don’t read your Bible every day, God is displeased.”
“God only hears the prayers of good people.”
“You must pray the right words for God to listen.”
“If you pray hard enough, God must give you what you ask.”
“The Bible is a rulebook meant to condemn you.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about God or yourself?

church-setting.note: Not everything taught at church is what Scripture teaches. Messages that distort God’s character can be examined in light of His Word.
church-setting.verse: “Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”

money.title: Toxic Messages from Money, Work & Status
money.intro: Please check any message you learned from finances, work, or your family’s circumstances.

items: “There will never be enough.”
“Anything I have could vanish tomorrow.”
“I must hold on to everything.”
“Asking for help means I’ve failed.”
“Life is never stable or safe.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “People with money are better than me.”
“Where I come from makes me less.”
“I don’t belong among successful people.”
“My clothes, car, or home show my worth.”
“Being poor means being lazy or bad.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “I am what I do for a living.”
“Without a job, I’m worthless.”
“Rest must be earned.”
“My value depends on how much I earn.”
“If I lose this job, I lose everything.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “I’m a failure because I lost my job.”
“I’ll never recover from this.”
“Others must think I’m useless.”
“I should be further along by now.”
“One setback means I’ve ruined my life.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “My debt proves I’m irresponsible.”
“I must hide my money problems.”
“I can never get out of this.”
“I don’t deserve anything nice.”
“Talking about money is shameful.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “Love is shown through things.”
“People like us never get ahead.”
“People like us don’t go to college.”
“Money is what causes all our fights.”
“Wealthy people can’t be trusted.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “I earned everything; others just didn’t try.”
“My worth depends on staying wealthy.”
“People only like me for my money.”
“I must never let anyone see me struggle.”
“Money can fix any problem.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “Retirement means I’m no longer useful.”
“Caring for others means my needs don’t count.”
“As a parent, I must provide everything.”
“I’m a burden now that I can’t work.”
“Needing help means losing my dignity.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

money.note: Our circumstances can teach powerful lessons about our worth, our security, and our future. Yet our value is not determined by what we earn or own. What was learned can be examined, questioned, and replaced with truth.
money.verse: “Look at the birds of the air… your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?”

church-upbringing.title: Toxic Messages from Church & Religion
church-upbringing.intro: Please check any message you learned from church, religious teaching, or your spiritual upbringing.

items: “God is angry with me.”
“God is waiting for me to mess up.”
“God loves me only when I’m good.”
“God is disappointed in me.”
“God is too busy to care about me.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “If I’m suffering, God is punishing me.”
“If I had more faith, I’d be healed.”
“God wants me healthy and wealthy.”
“If I give more, God must give me more.”
“Bad things mean I didn’t pray enough.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “I’ve sinned too much to be forgiven.”
“If I feel guilty, I must be guilty.”
“Good Christians always feel guilty.”
“I’ve committed the unpardonable sin.”
“My body and its desires are dirty.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “God forgives, but He never forgets.”
“I must pay for my sins.”
“I can never forgive myself.”
“Forgiving means I must trust them again.”
“I need a priest to be forgiven.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “I have to earn God’s acceptance.”
“I can never know if I’m really saved.”
“Going to church makes me right with God.”
“One more sin and God will give up on me.”
“I must suffer after death to be made pure.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “Doubt means I’m not a real Christian.”
“Strong emotions mean my faith is weak.”
“If I don’t feel close to God, He’s left me.”
“Depression means I don’t trust God.”
“Needing counseling means weak faith.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “Questioning my pastor is questioning God.”
“If my church teaches it, it must be biblical.”
“Good Christians don’t have problems.”
“My worth depends on how much I serve.”
“My needs and feelings don’t count.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

items: “Satan has more power over me than God.”
“Every problem I have is a spiritual attack.”
“I’m under a family curse I can’t escape.”
“I need a saint to reach God for me.”
“No tongues means I don’t have the Spirit.”
sections.p: If checked, what did you come to believe about yourself?

church-upbringing.note: Not everything taught in the name of God is the truth of God. Our beliefs about God can teach powerful lessons about our worth, our guilt, and our future. What was learned can be examined, questioned, tested against Scripture, and replaced with truth.
church-upbringing.verse: “Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”
